# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** 10  <sub>[v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008)</sub>

- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_
- **Family:** [Grandma Irving](../character/grandma-irving.md) (relative), [Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md) (parent)

## Appearance

Paul Irving is a small child for his age with exquisite, delicately refined facial features. He has big, very dark blue eyes and a halo of naturally curly chestnut-brown hair.

_Sources: [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021), [v2 XV The Beginning of Vacation P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P7](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0007), [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)_

## Personality

Paul Irving is described as a genius who is imaginative, fair-minded, and possesses occasional flashes of uncanny insight. He is a gentlemanly, cleanly child who acts as a perfect darling. Though known for his dreams and fancies, he is also very manly and capable of holding his own in games. Furthermore, he is kind to younger students, protecting them from larger boys and teaching them games, driven at times simply by the motive to make a joyful noise.

_Sources: [v2 VII The Pointing of Duty P7](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0007), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 VIII Marilla Adopts Twins P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road P3](../source/v02-c18.md#nw-v02-c18-p0003), [v2 XXIII Miss Lavendar’s Romance P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), +3 more_

## History

After moving from the [States](../codex/places.md#states) to live with his grandmother in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), Paul Irving became a pupil at the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school, forming a special connection with his teacher, [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md), who considered him her favorite student. Having promised his grandmother never to associate with anyone who swore, Paul possessed a vivid imagination, creating detailed imaginary friends who lived by the shore. Over time, Paul shared discussions about grief and imagination with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), hosted her for tea, and was introduced by her to Miss Lavendar at [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge). During a visit to [Echo Lodge](../codex/places.md#echo-lodge), Paul talked with Miss Lavendar about her imaginary dream-boy, unaware of her past romance with his father, [Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md). Later, as preparations for Miss Lavendar and Stephen's wedding got underway, Paul discussed the romantic turn of events with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md).

_Sources: [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P0](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0000), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P13](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0013), [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P23](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0023), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P0](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0000), [v2 XI Facts and Fancies P9](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0009), +27 more_

## Quotes

> “Yes; but if dryads are foolish they must take the consequences, just as if they were real people,” said Paul gravely. “Do you know what I think about the new moon, teacher? I think it is a little golden boat full of dreams.”
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XIX Just a Happy Day P30](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0030)

> "I’ve eaten enough to make anyone grow. I do hope, now that I’ve begun, I’ll keep on till I’m as tall as father. He is six feet, you know, Miss Lavendar."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024)

> "I think you would make a splendid mother. You have just the right look in your eyes . . . the look my little mother always had. I think it’s a pity you haven’t any boys of your own."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVII An Afternoon at the Stone House P58](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0058)

> "and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . ."
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)

> “Oh, Miss Shirley,” he cried excitedly, “you can’t think what has happened! Something so splendid. Father is here . . . just think of that! Father is here! Come right in. Father, this is my beautiful teacher. You know, father.”
>
> — Paul Irving — [v2 XXVIII The Prince Comes Back to the Enchanted Palace P21](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0021)

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--paul-irving.md)

[Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) is Paul's teacher, and she considers him her favorite pupil due to his imaginative compositions and gentle nature. Their connection quickly grows beyond the classroom into a close friendship through shared walks and visits, where they bond over discussions of family, grief, and imagination. [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) also helps introduce Paul to Miss Lavendar after learning of his father's past connection to her.
